header.tagline: Evolve a formula that explains your data, live and entirely in your browser.
restore.title: Continue where you left off?
restore.body: Your last run is saved in this browser: {summary}. It comes back paused, with its results.
restore.hint: Not now keeps it saved for your next visit; starting a new run replaces it.
data.title: 1. Data
data.samples.hint: evenly spaced across the X range; these are the points the run fits
data.formula.hint: Write formulas in x with Math functions and constants: sin(x), pow(x, 2), exp(-x*x), PI * x, or Math.sin(x).
data.sample.prompt: No file to hand, or unsure of the format?
data.csv.hint: Columns of numbers, usually with a header row. One column is the target to predict (the last one by default); every other column becomes an input (up to {max}). With a single input it is called x. Rows with empty cells or text are skipped.
csv.loaded: Loaded {file}: {count, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}}
csv.ignored: Only the first {max} input columns are used; ignored: {names}.
csv.preview.some: The first {shown} of {total} rows, as EquVolve reads them
csv.preview.all: All {total, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}}, as EquVolve reads them
csv.format.semicolonDecimalComma: Separated by semicolons, with decimal commas (1,5 is read as 1.5).
csv.format.tabDecimalComma: Separated by tabs, with decimal commas (1,5 is read as 1.5).
csv.skipped: Skipped {count, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}}: {details}.
csv.error.columns: The CSV needs at least two columns of numbers, separated by commas, semicolons or tabs.
settings.title: 2. Settings
setting.maxGenerations.label: Max Generations
setting.maxGenerations.hint: The run pauses after this many generations; raise it and press Resume to go on.
setting.targetR2.label: Target R²
setting.targetR2.hint: The run stops as soon as the best program fits this well (1 = perfect fit).
setting.populationSize.label: Population Size
setting.populationSize.hint: How many programs are tried at once. More can find harder formulas, but each generation is slower.
setting.crossoverRate.label: Crossover Rate
setting.crossoverRate.hint: How often (0–1) a new program combines parts of two good programs, instead of copying one.
setting.mutationRate.label: Mutation Rate
setting.mutationRate.hint: How often (0–1) a new program then gets a small random change.
setting.elitismRate.label: Elitism Rate
setting.elitismRate.hint: The share (0–1) of the best programs kept unchanged for the next generation.
setting.tournamentSize.label: Tournament Size
setting.tournamentSize.hint: Parents are chosen by letting this many random programs compete; larger favours the best more strongly.
setting.treeDepth.label: Initial Tree Depth
setting.treeDepth.hint: How deeply nested the random programs at the start may be.
setting.maxTreeDepth.label: Max Tree Depth
setting.maxTreeDepth.hint: How deeply nested any program may become (up to {limit}); stops programs growing without fitting better.
settings.speed.slow: Slow: one generation at a time
settings.speed.hint: Fast runs many generations between screen updates. Slow is for watching each step.
operators.title: Operators
operators.hint: The building blocks programs may use. Pick what matches your data: Trigonometric for waves, Exp / Log for growth, decay or bell curves, Rational for division. A few fitting operators usually beat Everything.
advanced.title: Advanced settings
advanced.hint: The defaults work well for most data. These are for exploring how genetic programming behaves.
advanced.linearScaling.hint: Lets every program be stretched and shifted (a + b·f(x)) to fit the data, so evolution only has to find the right shape.
advanced.constantOptimization.hint: Each generation, fine-tune the numbers inside a random 10% of programs (such as the 1/3 in exp(x/3)). Experimental and off by default: in our benchmark it did not improve results.
run.fix: {count, plural, one {Fix this to continue:} other {Fix these # problems to continue:}}
run.missingOperators: Your formula uses {ops}, which {count, plural, one {is} other {are}} not ticked under Operators, so a run can only approximate it.
run.unsupported: {names} {count, plural, one {is} other {are}} not available as an operator, so a run can only approximate it.
results.title: 3. Results
results.r2.hint: R² measures the fit: 1 is perfect, 0 is no better than always guessing the average, and below 0 is worse than that.
replay.play.label: Play replay
replay.pause.label: Pause replay
export.copyFailed: Copy failed: select the text manually
chart.fit.multi: Fit: predicted vs actual for each row; points on the diagonal are predicted exactly
chart.fit.single: Fit: data and best program
chart.progress: Progress per generation (log scale of 1 − R²): best median target
tree.title: Expression tree
tree.label: Expression tree for y = {expression}
tree.hint: Each node is labelled with its operator, variable or number: operators are orange, variables green and numbers khaki. Point at a number to see all its digits.

status.restored: Restored session at generation {generation}. Press Resume to continue.
status.broughtBack: Brought back the run at generation {generation}.
status.maxGenerations: Stopped at Max Generations ({generation}). Increase Max Generations and press Resume to continue.
resume.perfect: The best program fits the data perfectly, so there is nothing left to improve. Press New run to search again from scratch.
resume.targetR2: The best program already reaches Target R² {target}. To keep improving it, raise Target R² and press Resume; or press New run to search again from scratch.
resume.maxGenerations: The run is at Max Generations ({max}). To continue it, raise Max Generations and press Resume; or press New run to search again from scratch.

share.contents: It contains the settings, the data and the best program, but not the population.
share.loadedRun: Loaded a shared run: R² {r2} after {generation, plural, one {# generation} other {# generations}}.
share.datasetMissing: Its dataset was too large to include; upload it to run.
share.pressStart: Press Start Evolution to evolve it yourself.
share.unreadable: This share link could not be read. It may be incomplete; try copying it again.
validation.populationSize: Population Size must be a whole number of at least 2.
validation.maxGenerations: Max Generations must be a whole number of at least 1.
validation.targetR2: Target R² must be a number no greater than 1.
validation.mutationRate: Mutation Rate must be between 0 and 1.
validation.crossoverRate: Crossover Rate must be between 0 and 1.
validation.elitismRate: Elitism Rate must be between 0 and 1.
validation.tournamentSize: Tournament Size must be a whole number of at least 1.
validation.treeDepth: Initial Tree Depth must be a whole number between 1 and {max}.
validation.maxTreeDepth: Max Tree Depth must be a whole number between Initial Tree Depth and {max}.
validation.datasetRows: Upload a CSV dataset with at least 2 valid rows.
validation.datasetColumns: The dataset needs between 1 and {max} input columns.
validation.datasetValues: Every dataset row needs a numeric value for each input column.
validation.xRange: X Range minimum must be smaller than the maximum.
validation.sampleCount: Sample Points must be a whole number between 2 and {max}.
validation.formulaValues: Formula produces fewer than 2 finite values in the X Range.
validation.constantTarget: Target values are constant; R² is undefined for a constant target.
formula.error.syntax: it is not a complete expression; check its brackets and operators
